guide.title: Allergen guide

rule: Knoops: checked by hand against the guide's 'Cereals containing gluten' column. Oats, including gluten free oats, and 'may contain traces' count as gluten.

reviewed.by: Claude, checked against the rendered guide pages

notices.label: Cross-contact
notices.text: It is important to let you know that we cannot guarantee any of our products are suitable for those with allergies due to a high risk of cross contamination.

notices.label: Cross-contact
notices.text: Our vegan chocolates and bakery items are made to a vegan recipe but are not suitable for those with a dairy allergy as there is a risk of cross contamination in our stores due to the number of chocolates we use.

notices.label: What the guide covers
notices.text: This guide will provide nutritional and allergen information for core product range in our Knoops Stores and our retail range.

headline: Not oat, barista almond or coconut milk.
tips: Pick any chocolate except 38% Oat M*ilk: the guide marks it as made with gluten free oats.
Milk: whole, semi-skimmed, skimmed, lacto-free, (barista) soya or organic hazelnut. Not oat, or the barista almond or coconut milks, which the guide marks as containing oats.
gaps: Knoops doesn't call anything gluten free, apart from 'Gluten Free Ice Cream Cones', which its own guide marks as may contain traces of gluten.
The guide is from March 2024 and has no end date. Recipes may have changed since.
The guide marks the cannoli as containing no gluten cereals. Cannoli shells are usually made with wheat flour, so check in store (this is the app's caution, not Knoops' words).
The guide lists chocolates and milks separately, not finished drinks, so it doesn't say how each drink is made.
